title: Tracing the Future Soldier's Tech Stack
gist: Cogs of War staff survey of fielded Army and DARPA soldier technologies: current capabilities (night vision, health wearables, freeze-dried plasma) are modest, but DARPA/Army proposals point to neuromodulation, brain-machine interfaces, next-gen headsets, smart combat shirts, and even epigenetic engineering and enhanced red blood cells.

insights.claim: Existing fielded soldier capabilities remain relatively modest: night vision is decades old, while health and performance wearables are fielded and becoming more common.
insights.speaker: Cogs of War Staff
insights.so_what: Soldier-tech market is still early; wearable health monitoring is the adoption beachhead.

insights.claim: Freeze-dried plasma began as a special operations tool and has recently been introduced into the joint medical force.
insights.speaker: Cogs of War Staff
insights.so_what: Shows a diffusion path from SOF to the broader force that suppliers can target.
insights.quote: Freeze-dried plasma started as a special operations tool and has recently been introduced into the joint medical force.

insights.claim: The Army awarded agreements last fall for the Soldier Borne Mission Command program for next-generation soldier-worn headsets.
insights.speaker: Cogs of War Staff
insights.so_what: Identifies an active procurement line for soldier-worn AR/headset vendors.

insights.claim: The Army awarded a company a contract for a physiological metrics monitoring combat shirt intended to replace bulky existing monitoring devices.
insights.speaker: Cogs of War Staff
insights.so_what: Textile-integrated biometric sensing is moving to contract stage.

insights.claim: DARPA has an ongoing program on non-invasive neuromodulation to limit the effects of sleep deprivation, and previously explored brain-machine interfaces for soldiers teaming with drones, cyber systems, or computers.
insights.speaker: Cogs of War Staff
insights.so_what: Neurotech is a defense R&D frontier with potential dual-use spillover.

insights.claim: DARPA started a program in 2021 to invent small wearable eyeglasses for night vision and completed a program for lightweight armor against ballistic and blast threats.
insights.speaker: Cogs of War Staff
insights.so_what: Night-vision miniaturization and lightweight armor are near-term upgrade cycles.

insights.claim: DARPA has put out proposals for genetic and cellular-level enhancements, including epigenetic engineering that changes body function without permanent DNA modification and enhanced red blood cells that release compounds to improve performance and survival.
insights.speaker: Cogs of War Staff
insights.so_what: Biotech-based soldier enhancement is a long-dated, ethically fraught but funded research area.
